metadata.title: Network Wireless Access

metadata.remarks:
Network Wireless Access defines the capability to provide safe and controlled network connectivity over broadcast media. Wireless access introduces increased exposure due to its shared medium and therefore requires strong admission controls, isolation, encryption, and continuous context awareness.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for SSPPs, standards, procedures, guidelines, and assurance related to wireless connectivity. Controls are scoped to wireless-specific sub-capabilities to reflect the unique risks of broadcast access.

components.title: Wireless Admission
components.description: Controlled association of devices and identities to wireless networks.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Enforce approved authorizations for wireless network access.
Authenticate users or devices prior to wireless network access.

components.title: Broadcast Isolation
components.description: Isolation of wireless clients to prevent unauthorized peer-to-peer communication.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Isolate wireless clients to limit unintended data exposure.

components.title: Roaming Context
components.description: Management of context and policy as devices move across wireless access points.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Maintain access controls across wireless roaming events.

components.title: Wireless Encryption
components.description: Protection of wireless communications using approved cryptographic mechanisms.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Employ cryptographic mechanisms to protect wireless data in transit.
Use strong cryptographic protocols to establish secure wireless associations.
